title: The covering number C(12, 6, 4) is 41
summary: A $t$-$(v,k,λ)$ covering is a collection of $k$-subsets (blocks) of a $v$-set such that every $t$-subset of points lies in at least $λ$ blocks; the covering number $C_λ(v,k,t)$ is the least number of blocks in such a collection, and one writes $C(v,k,t)$ when $λ=1$. The recorded bounds for $C(12,6,4)$ have been $40 \le C(12,6,4) \le 41$. We show that no $4$-$(12,6,1)$ covering with $40$ blocks exists, and hence that $C(12,6,4)=41$. A counting argument shows that in a hypothetical $40$-block covering every point lies in exactly $20$ blocks, the link of every point is an optimal $3$-$(11,5,1)$…
